<b>Слуховая труба</b> (≈ 36 мм) идёт от: The auditory tube (about 36 mm) runs from the anterior wall forward, medially, and down to the nasopharynx. Its back third is bony; the front two-thirds are cartilaginous and normally closed. Behind, the cavity opens through the aditus into the mastoid antrum and the air cells of the mastoid process. That is why otitis media can spread into mastoiditis.
<b>Латеральная (перепончатая) стенка</b>: The lateral (membranous) wall is the eardrum plus the bony plate above it that separates the epitympanic recess from the ear canal. The eardrum measures about 9 × 10 mm and is about 0.1 mm thick. It is tilted and drawn inward like a funnel toward the umbo, the tip of the handle of the malleus.
<b>Медиальная (лабиринтная) стенка</b> о: The medial (labyrinthine) wall separates the cavity from the inner ear. In the middle is the promontory, a bulge made by the basal turn of the cochlea. Above it is the oval window with the stapes; below and behind it is the round window, closed by the secondary tympanic membrane. The facial canal runs above the oval window, and higher still is the bulge of the lateral semicircular canal.
<b>Верхняя (покрышечная) стенка</b> — то: The superior (tegmental) wall is a thin plate of temporal bone forming the roof of the cavity. Above it lie the middle cranial fossa and the temporal lobe of the brain. That is why a suppurative ear infection is occasionally complicated by meningitis or a brain abscess.
<b>Нижняя (яремная) стенка</b> — узкое д: The inferior (jugular) wall is the narrow floor of the cavity above the bulb of the internal jugular vein. The plate can be very thin, and sometimes it has a gap.
<b>Передняя (сонная) стенка</b> отделяет: The anterior (carotid) wall separates the cavity from the canal of the internal carotid artery. Its upper part has two openings: the semicanal of the tensor tympani and, below it, the entrance to the auditory tube.
<b>Задняя (сосцевидная) стенка.</b> Ввер: The posterior (mastoid) wall. At its top is the aditus to the mastoid antrum; below that is the pyramidal eminence, from which the stapedius tendon emerges. The facial nerve descends within the wall, and the chorda tympani enters the cavity from it.
<b>Острый средний отит.</b> Гной в полос: Acute otitis media. Pus in the cavity pushes the eardrum outward. It is red and cloudy, and the handle of the malleus and the cone of light are no longer visible. Pain, fever, and reduced hearing; most common in children after a cold. It usually clears in a few days; severe cases are treated with antibiotics.
<b>Экссудативный отит.</b> За перепонкой: Otitis media with effusion. Fluid sits behind the eardrum without acute inflammation. The eardrum is amber, and an air–fluid level and air bubbles show through it. Hearing is reduced, but there is no pain. It is a common cause of hearing loss in children; if the fluid persists for months, ventilation tubes are placed in the eardrum.
<b>Втянутая перепонка.</b> Труба не откр: Retracted eardrum. The tube does not open, air in the cavity is gradually absorbed by the lining, and the pressure falls. The eardrum is sucked inward: the handle looks shorter and more horizontal, the short process sticks out, and the cone of light breaks up or disappears.
<b>Перфорация</b> — отверстие в натянуто: A perforation is a hole in the tense part after an infection or injury (a slap over the ear, a pressure change, a cotton swab). The pink medial wall shows through it. Small holes usually heal on their own within a few weeks; large ones are closed surgically (myringoplasty).
<b>Барабанная полость</b> — щель объёмом: The tympanic cavity is an air-filled slit of about 1 cm³ between the eardrum and the inner ear. It is shaped like a narrow drum, about 15 mm tall and 2–6 mm deep (from the umbo of the eardrum to the promontory is only about 2 mm). It holds a chain of three ossicles, two muscles, and the chorda tympani. Choose a part or one of the six walls — each has its own neighbors.
<b>У ребёнка</b> слуховая труба вдвое ко: In a child the auditory tube is half as long (about 18 mm), wider, and almost horizontal, and its cartilage is softer. Mucus and germs from the nasopharynx easily reach the middle ear, which is why ear infections are so common in children. By age 7 the tube lengthens and tilts downward.
<b>Приём Вальсальвы.</b> Выдох с закрыты: The Valsalva maneuver. Exhaling with the mouth closed and the nose pinched raises the pressure in the nasopharynx, and air bursts into the tube. The pressure is equalized and the eardrum moves back into place. Blow gently: a forceful exhalation can damage the eardrum and the windows of the inner ear.
Три косточки размером с рисовое зерно не: Three ossicles the size of a grain of rice keep sound from bouncing off the fluid of the inner ear, two tiny muscles damp loud noise, and the auditory tube equalizes pressure when we swallow.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The middle ear is an air-filled cavity in the temporal bone between the external ear canal and the inner ear. It has three levels: the epitympanic recess with the head of the malleus and the body of the incus, the middle part facing the eardrum, and the lower recess above the bulb of the jugular vein. The cavity is lined with mucosa and connected to the nasopharynx by the auditory tube and, at the back, to the air cells of the mastoid process.

The ossicles are linked by true joints and suspended by ligaments. The malleus and incus rock as one unit around an axis through the anterior process of the malleus and the short process of the incus, while the stapes moves in the oval window like a piston.

How it works

Without the middle ear, only about 0.1% of sound energy would pass from air into the fluid of the cochlea. The large eardrum and the ossicular lever concentrate pressure onto the small oval window and boost it about 22-fold. The round window bulges the opposite way, giving the cochlear fluid room to move.

The auditory tube ventilates the cavity and equalizes pressure. The palatal muscles open it during swallowing and yawning; at rest it is closed — otherwise you would hear your own breathing and voice far too loudly.

Medicine

  • Otitis media is the most common reason young children see a doctor. Acute otitis usually clears on its own or with antibiotics; complications include perforation, mastoiditis, and, rarely, meningitis.
  • Otitis media with effusion means fluid behind the eardrum and hearing loss without pain. If it lasts for months, ventilation tubes are placed, and sometimes the adenoids that block the tube openings are removed.
  • Otosclerosis is bone overgrowth around the footplate of the stapes, which stops moving. Hearing declines gradually; surgery helps — the stapes is replaced with a prosthesis.
  • Cholesteatoma is a pocket of skin growing into the cavity, usually from the pars flaccida. It slowly destroys the ossicles and walls, so it is removed surgically.
  • Facial nerve palsy (Bell palsy): the nerve swells inside its narrow canal. Besides the face, taste (chorda tympani) and the stapedius are affected — sounds seem too loud.

Simplifications

  • The cavity is enlarged about 5 times, and the walls are shown as translucent plates without thickness; the mucosa, ligaments of the ossicles, folds, and vessels of the cavity are not shown. Ossicle vibrations are exaggerated many thousands of times (in reality they are fractions of a micrometer) and slowed down. Pressure changes in the Pressure mode are simplified.

  • 1–4 mode · Esc clear selection

<b>Слуховые косточки</b> — молоточек, на: The auditory ossicles — malleus, incus, and stapes — are the smallest bones in the body (the stapes is about 3 mm long). The handle of the malleus is woven into the eardrum; its head sits in the epitympanic recess, jointed to the incus. The long process of the incus meets the stapes, whose footplate closes the oval window.
<b>Две самые маленькие мышцы тела.</b> М: The two smallest muscles in the body. The tensor tympani (nerve V₃) lies above the auditory tube; its tendon turns around the cochleariform process and pulls the handle of the malleus inward. The stapedius (nerve VII) hides in the pyramidal eminence of the posterior wall and pulls on the neck of the stapes. Both stiffen the chain against loud sound.
<b>Лицевой нерв (VII)</b> идёт в костном: The facial nerve (VII) runs in a bony canal above the oval window, then descends in the posterior wall to the stylomastoid foramen. It gives off the nerve to the stapedius and the chorda tympani, which crosses the cavity between the malleus and incus and carries taste from the front two-thirds of the tongue. The tympanic plexus (IX) lies on the promontory.
<b>Зачем нужны косточки.</b> Из воздуха: Why we need the ossicles. Going from air into the fluid of the inner ear, sound would be almost entirely reflected. The eardrum (about 55 mm²) funnels pressure onto the stapes footplate (about 3.2 mm²), an area 17 times smaller, and the ossicular lever adds ×1.3. In all, pressure rises about 22-fold (about 27 dB). Turn up the volume: above about 85 dB the reflex kicks in.
<b>Акустический рефлекс.</b> На громкий: The acoustic reflex. In response to loud sound, the stapedius muscles on both sides contract within 25–150 ms, pulling the stapes back and stiffening the chain, which damps low frequencies by 10–20 dB. It guards against prolonged noise, but a gunshot is faster than the reflex. With facial nerve palsy, ordinary sounds feel painfully loud (hyperacusis).
<b>Давление по обе стороны перепонки.</b: Pressure on both sides of the eardrum. Air in the cavity is absorbed by its lining, and only the auditory tube can replace it. The tube is closed and opens for a split second when you swallow or yawn, pulled open by the tensor veli palatini. As a plane descends, the eardrum is pushed inward. Move the slider and press “Swallow.”
<b>Нормальная перепонка</b> (правое ухо): A normal eardrum (right ear) is pearly gray and translucent. The handle of the malleus shows through it, running from the short process down and back to the umbo. From the umbo the cone of light — the otoscope lamp’s reflection — points forward and down (5 o’clock in the right ear, 7 in the left). Above the short process is the pars flaccida; below it, the pars tensa.
<b>Труба «заперта».</b> При перепаде бол: The tube is “locked.” Above a difference of about 90 mm Hg, the walls of the tube are pressed shut and swallowing no longer opens it. The Valsalva maneuver helps — a gentle exhalation with the mouth closed and the nose pinched. Swallow and yawn from the start of the descent; with a runny nose the maneuver can push mucus into the ear.
